title: Hip replacement
what: The surgeon replaces a worn-out hip joint with an artificial one. It is usually done under spinal anesthesia or general anesthesia.
why: Most often for severe hip arthritis, when pain makes it hard to walk and sleep and treatment does not help. Also after a broken hip.
duration: surgery usually takes 1 to 2 hours; the hospital stay is usually 3 to 7 days
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. The doctor will tell you what to stop and when
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes
If you ever had blood clots in your legs
If you or your relatives ever had problems with anesthesia
Bad teeth, skin sores, or infections. These are treated before surgery

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, an X-ray, and check-ups with a general doctor and other doctors. Your clinic will give you the list.

prepare.title: Anesthesiologist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthesiologist will talk with you about your pain relief.

prepare.title: Your home
prepare.text: Ahead of time, remove rugs and cables from the floor, get a high chair, and have a walker or crutches ready.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food from the evening before, and no drinks for a few hours before. Your clinic will give you the exact time.

bring: Your referral, test results, and X-rays
Closed, comfortable shoes with non-slip soles
Things for a few days in hospital
Crutches or a walker, if you were asked to bring your own
steps: On the day of surgery, you change your clothes and a thin tube is put into a vein
In the operating room you get pain relief: an injection in the back or general anesthesia
The surgeon makes a cut on the side or back of the hip
The damaged parts of the joint are removed and the artificial joint is put in
The wound is stitched. Sometimes a thin tube is left in to drain fluid
You wake up in the recovery room, then you are moved to your room
feel: After surgery, pain in the hip. You will get pain medicine
After the injection in the back, you cannot feel your legs for a while. This passes
In the first days, weakness and getting tired quickly
after: You are usually helped to stand with a walker on day 1 or 2
Do the exercises your physical therapist shows you
You are usually given medicine or stockings against blood clots, as your doctor plans
In the first weeks, do not sit on low seats, cross your legs, or bend far forward. Your surgeon will give you the exact rules
You usually need to walk with support for several weeks
Full recovery usually takes several months
red_flags: Swelling and pain in the calf. This may be a blood clot
Sudden shortness of breath or chest pain: call emergency services right away
A fever above 38 degrees, redness, pus, or fluid from the wound
Sudden strong pain in the hip, or your leg looks shorter or turned: see a doctor right away

faq.q: How long does an artificial hip last?
faq.a: Usually 15 to 20 years or more. A lot depends on your weight, activity, and care.

faq.q: When can I walk after hip replacement?
faq.a: With a walker, usually after 1 to 2 days. Without support, after several weeks, when your doctor allows.

reminders.text: Surgery tomorrow. Pack your things, documents, X-rays, and list of medicines. Eat and drink only until the time your clinic gave you.
